nodes.label: Nodes
nodes.blurb: The machines that run VMs, with their provider and free capacity.

vms.label: VMs
vms.blurb: Every VM, the node it runs on, and its management hostname for SSH.

disks.label: Disks
disks.blurb: Standalone disks that outlive VMs. Attach a disk to a VM to mount it; it is kept when the VM is deleted.

keys.label: SSH keys
keys.blurb: Stored public keys. Keys of the hub machine are always listed and preselected when you create a VM.

devices.label: Devices
devices.blurb: WireGuard client devices. A device reaches every VM by its management hostname.

networks.label: Networks
networks.blurb: Private networks that VMs can join. VMs on the same network reach each other as NAME.NETWORK.internal.

settings.label: Settings
settings.blurb: Hub address, token and defaults for guests.

nodes.emptyBody: A node registers with the hub as soon as it is started with the hub's URL and token.
nodes.providerHint: vz for a Mac (Apple Silicon), firecracker or cloud-hypervisor for a Linux host (amd64 with KVM).

vms.emptyBody: A VM boots on the node you pick when creating it. SSH goes through a WireGuard device, using the VM's management hostname.
vms.deleteBody: The VM is stopped and its disks are removed from the node. This cannot be undone.
vms.stopBody: Power off immediately? Unsaved data in the VM is lost.

create.title: New VM
create.dataDisksHint: Attach existing disks or create new ones. They are formatted as ext4 on first use and mounted at the mount path.
create.networksHint: VMs on the same network reach each other as NAME.NETWORK.internal.

keys.emptyBody: Add your public key once, e.g. the contents of {file}.
keys.hubHint: From ~/.ssh on the hub machine, read again on every start
keys.publicKeyHint: The contents of your {ext} file, e.g. {cmd}.
keys.deleteBody: The key will no longer be offered for new VMs. VMs already created with it keep it.

node.capacityHint: Used means reserved by VMs on this node, out of the capacity the node offers.
node.notReported: Not reported by this node yet.
node.configHint: The node's config file as it reported it on connect. The hub token is never sent.
node.hubAddressHint: Use localhost for the hub's own Mac, or a LAN IP when nodes reach the hub differently.
node.saveHint: Save as ~/.vm-manager/node.json on the node and start ./bin/vm-manager-node
node.copyFailed: Copy failed; select the text manually.
node.deleteBody: The node is removed from the hub.
node.deleteBodyOnline: The node is removed from the hub and disconnected; if it keeps running it reconnects and appears again.
node.installHint: Run this on the machine (on Linux as a user with sudo). Running it again updates the node and keeps its VMs; they restart with the node.
node.providerMismatch: Hypervisor differs from the one chosen when adding the node: {error}.
node.updateBody: {count} running VM will restart. Continue? | {count} running VMs will restart. Continue?
node.updateByHand: This node was started by hand. Run the install command below to update it.

vm.networksHint: Networks this VM is attached to besides management. Reach it from other members as NAME.NETWORK.internal.
vm.restartBody: The VM will restart to apply the network change.
vm.attachedDisksHint: Standalone disks mounted in this VM. They stay when the VM is deleted.
vm.detachBody: The disk is unmounted and kept. It can be attached again once the node has released it.
vm.restartDisksBody: The VM will restart to apply the disk change.

devices.emptyBody: Add a device for each laptop or phone that should reach VMs as NAME.mgmt.internal.
devices.createdHint: This config contains the device's private key, so treat it as a secret. Import it into WireGuard now; you can download it again from the Devices list.
devices.deleteBody: The device loses access to all VMs immediately.
devices.qrFailed: The QR code could not be generated. Use the config text or the download.
devices.onHub: This device is the hub machine
devices.onHubHint: Its WireGuard config connects via 127.0.0.1, which the WireGuard app on the hub machine needs.

networks.emptyBody: Create a network to let VMs reach each other privately.
networks.subnetHint: CIDR, e.g. 10.20.0.0/24. Leave empty to pick one automatically.
networks.deleteBody: The network and its subnet are removed.

settings.setupBanner: Setup not finished – set the client endpoint
settings.endpointHint: Address devices and nodes use to reach the hub
settings.storageEndpointHint: host:port nodes use to reach the storage server. Leave empty for the client endpoint with the storage port.
settings.endpointChangeBody: No device keeps the old address in its config.|One device keeps the old address in its config; download it again.|{count} devices keep the old address in their configs; download them again.
settings.storageChangeBody: No VM uses a disk.|One VM with disks gets the new storage address and restarts.|{count} VMs with disks get the new storage address and restart.
settings.tokenChangeBody: Nodes need the new token in their node.json the next time they connect.
settings.guestMTUHint: applied to VMs on their next DHCP lease or reboot (576–9000)

updates.manual: Update available. Set VMM_VERSION={version} in deploy/.env and run in the checkout:
updates.upToDate: The hub is up to date.
updates.unavailable: The hub did not answer with its update status.

disks.emptyBody: Create a disk and attach it to a VM. Disks survive deleting the VM.
disks.sizeHint: Can only be grown later, not shrunk.
disks.copyWarning: The disk may still be written by a VM. The copy is then only crash-consistent.
disks.growHint: Currently {size} GB. A disk can only grow.
disks.growRestartBody: The VM will restart to see the larger disk.
disks.releaseBody: Node {node} has not confirmed that it let go of this disk. If it is gone for good, release it now. Anything it still writes to the disk is lost.
disks.deleteBody: The disk and its data are removed. This cannot be undone.
disks.orphansHint: Files on the storage host that belong to no disk. They are not deleted automatically.
